title: Power Sums Generate the Symmetric Subalgebra in Characteristic 0
description: Upgrades the parent's reverse Newton membership statement (each eₖ lies in the ℚ-subalgebra generated by the power sums) to the sharp subalgebra equality Algebra.adjoin ℚ (Set.range (psum σ ℚ)) = symmetricSubalgebra σ ℚ for every finite σ. The ℚ-subalgebra generated by the power sums is exactly the symmetric subalgebra — neither bigger (every power sum is symmetric) nor smaller (every symmetric polynomial is a ℚ-polynomial in the power sums). The hard inclusion composes Mathlib's fundamental theorem of symmetric polynomials (esymmAlgHom_surjective: every symmetric polynomial is a ℚ-polynomial in the elementary symmetric polynomials) with the parent's reverse Newton identity (esymm_mem_adjoin_psum: every eₖ is a ℚ-polynomial in the power sums); the easy inclusion is symmetry of the power sums. A corollary, isSymmetric_mem_psumAdjoin, restates the hard direction as 'every symmetric polynomial over ℚ is a polynomial in the power sums'.

meta.author: Lean Genius

mathlibDependencies.description: Fundamental theorem of symmetric polynomials: the algebra homomorphism esymmAlgHom σ R n (sending Xᵢ ↦ eᵢ₊₁) onto the symmetric subalgebra is surjective once n ≥ |σ|. This supplies that every symmetric polynomial is a polynomial in e₁,…,e_{|σ|} — the entry point of the hard inclusion.
(esymmAlgHom σ R n p).val = aeval (fun i ↦ esymm σ R (i+1)) p; converts the abstract surjectivity witness into the concrete equation p = aeval (e_{i+1}) q used to place p in an adjoin of the eₖ.

Algebra.adjoin R (Set.range f) = (aeval f).range; identifies the image of aeval (fun i ↦ esymm σ ℚ (i+1)) with the subalgebra generated by those elementary symmetric polynomials, so the surjectivity witness directly gives subalgebra membership.
Every power sum psum σ ℚ n is a symmetric polynomial; gives the easy inclusion psumAdjoin ≤ symmetricSubalgebra via Algebra.adjoin_le.

If a generating set is contained in a subalgebra S, then the adjoin is ≤ S. Used twice: to bound psumAdjoin by the symmetric subalgebra (easy inclusion), and to bound adjoin ℚ (range eₖ) by psumAdjoin (final step of the hard inclusion).

originalContributions: psum_adjoin_eq_symmetric: for every finite σ, Algebra.adjoin ℚ (Set.range (psum σ ℚ)) = symmetricSubalgebra σ ℚ. Mathlib has the fundamental theorem (the eₖ generate the symmetric subalgebra) and, via the parent, the reverse Newton identity, but no statement that the power sums generate the symmetric subalgebra. overview.historicalContext:
That the power sums $p_1,p_2,\dots$ generate the ring of symmetric functions over a field of characteristic $0$ is a classical theorem (Macdonald, *Symmetric Functions and Hall Polynomials*, I.2). It is the precise statement behind the informal claim 'every symmetric polynomial is a polynomial in the power sums.' The result splits into two halves that come from genuinely different places: the *fundamental theorem of symmetric polynomials* (the elementary symmetric polynomials $e_k$ generate the symmetric subalgebra) and *Newton's identities in reverse* (each $e_k$ is itself a $\mathbb{Q}$-polynomial in the power sums). Composing them is the content of this entry.

The parent entry proved the second half as a *membership* statement, $e_k\in\mathrm{adjoin}_{\mathbb{Q}}(\mathrm{range}\,p)$. Mathlib supplies the first half as `esymmAlgHom_surjective`. This entry combines the two into the sharp subalgebra *equality* — the cleanest formal expression of 'the power sums generate the symmetric functions in characteristic 0.'
overview.problemStatement:
**Open Question** (parent entry, conclusion §openQuestions, first item): *Upgrade the membership statement to a subalgebra equality $\mathrm{adjoin}_{\mathbb{Q}}(\mathrm{range}\,p) = \mathrm{symmetricSubalgebra}\,\sigma\,\mathbb{Q}$, combining $e_k\in\mathrm{adjoin}_{\mathbb{Q}}(\mathrm{range}\,p)$ with Mathlib's fundamental theorem of symmetric polynomials.*

**Answer**: For every finite $\sigma$,
$$\mathrm{Algebra.adjoin}\;\mathbb{Q}\;(\mathrm{range}\,(\mathrm{psum}\,\sigma\,\mathbb{Q})) = \mathrm{symmetricSubalgebra}\,\sigma\,\mathbb{Q}.$$
The $\le$ inclusion is symmetry of the power sums; the $\ge$ inclusion composes $\texttt{esymmAlgHom\_surjective}$ with the parent's $\texttt{esymm\_mem\_adjoin\_psum}$.
overview.text: The power sums generate exactly the symmetric subalgebra over ℚ: adjoin ℚ (range psum) = symmetricSubalgebra σ ℚ for finite σ. The hard inclusion composes Mathlib's fundamental theorem (esymm generate the symmetric subalgebra) with the parent's reverse Newton identity (esymm ∈ adjoin psum).
overview.proofStrategy:
**Easy inclusion (psumAdjoin_le_symmetric).** `Algebra.adjoin_le` reduces to showing each generator is symmetric: for the generator $p_n$, `psum_isSymmetric σ ℚ n` gives membership in `symmetricSubalgebra σ ℚ`.

**Hard inclusion (symmetric_le_psumAdjoin).** Fix a symmetric $p$ and set $n=|\sigma|$. By `esymmAlgHom_surjective` (with $n\ge|\sigma|$, here equality), the algebra hom onto the symmetric subalgebra is surjective, so there is $q\in\mathbb{Q}[X_1,\dots,X_n]$ with $\mathrm{esymmAlgHom}\,q = \langle p, h_p\rangle$. Taking values and using `esymmAlgHom_apply` gives $\mathrm{aeval}\,(i\mapsto e_{i+1})\,q = p$. Then `Algebra.adjoin_range_eq_range_aeval` identifies $(\mathrm{aeval}\,f).\mathrm{range}$ with $\mathrm{adjoin}_{\mathbb{Q}}(\mathrm{range}\,f)$, so $p\in\mathrm{adjoin}_{\mathbb{Q}}\{e_1,\dots,e_n\}$. Finally `Algebra.adjoin_le` plus the parent's `esymm_mem_adjoin_psum σ ℚ (i+1)` (each $e_{i+1}$ is in the power-sum subalgebra) yields $p\in\mathrm{adjoin}_{\mathbb{Q}}(\mathrm{range}\,p)$.

**Equality (psum_adjoin_eq_symmetric).** `le_antisymm` of the two inclusions.
keyInsights: The result is a genuine SYNTHESIS, not a single deduction: the two inclusions draw on two unrelated theorems. The fundamental theorem of symmetric polynomials supplies 'symmetric ⟹ polynomial in the eₖ' and the reverse Newton identity supplies 'eₖ ⟹ polynomial in the power sums'; chaining them is exactly what turns the parent's membership statement into a generation (equality) statement.

Phrasing as a subalgebra equality is the sharp form: it says the power sums generate neither more nor less than the symmetric functions. The ≤ direction (power sums are symmetric) prevents overshoot; the ≥ direction (every symmetric polynomial is reachable) prevents undershoot.

The surjectivity witness q lives in MvPolynomial (Fin n) ℚ; Algebra.adjoin_range_eq_range_aeval is the precise bridge turning 'p = aeval (eₖ) q' into 'p ∈ adjoin ℚ (range eₖ)' without manually expanding q as a sum of monomials.

Fixing the base ring to ℚ (rather than a general ℚ-algebra) is what makes both sides subalgebras over the same field, so le_antisymm produces an honest equality of objects of the same type. The characteristic-0 content is inherited entirely from the parent's reverse Newton identity.

The finiteness of σ enters through the fundamental theorem, which needs exactly |σ| elementary symmetric polynomials to be surjective; taking n = Fintype.card σ makes the hypothesis n ≥ |σ| an equality and the application is le_rfl.

conclusion.summary: Proves the sharp subalgebra equality Algebra.adjoin ℚ (Set.range (psum σ ℚ)) = symmetricSubalgebra σ ℚ for every finite σ: the power sums generate exactly the symmetric subalgebra over ℚ. The easy inclusion is symmetry of the power sums; the hard inclusion composes Mathlib's fundamental theorem of symmetric polynomials (esymmAlgHom_surjective) with the parent's reverse Newton identity (esymm_mem_adjoin_psum). 0 sorries, 0 axioms.
conclusion.implications:
**For the gallery's Newton–Girard chain**: completes the generation story. The parent showed each eₖ lies in the power-sum subalgebra (membership); this entry shows the two families generate the *same* subalgebra, which is moreover the full symmetric subalgebra. Together with Mathlib's fundamental theorem this is the characteristic-0 'power sums = symmetric functions' theorem, fully machine-checked.

**Methodologically**: demonstrates the 'compose two generation theorems through adjoin_range_eq_range_aeval' pattern — convert a surjectivity witness into adjoin membership, then bound that adjoin by a third subalgebra via adjoin_le. A reusable template for 'family X generates the same subalgebra as family Y' results.
openQuestions: Make the change of basis explicit and effective: extract from esymmAlgHom_surjective the actual ℚ-polynomial expressing a given symmetric polynomial in the power sums, e.g. via the determinantal formula k!·eₖ = det(power-sum matrix).
Generalise the equality from ℚ to an arbitrary characteristic-0 field (or a torsion-free ℚ-algebra base), tracking where the symmetricSubalgebra-over-the-base hypothesis is used.

crossReferences.description: Direct parent: proves the reverse Newton membership esymm σ R k ∈ Algebra.adjoin ℚ (Set.range (psum σ R)). This entry answers its first stated open question by upgrading membership to the subalgebra equality, using esymm_mem_adjoin_psum as the second half of the hard inclusion.
Grandparent: the general Newton–Girard recurrence psum_recurrence / mul_esymm_recurrence on which the reverse direction (and hence this generation statement) is built.
Root of this sub-branch: Maclaurin inequalities via elementary symmetric polynomials.

Vieta's formulas give the elementary symmetric polynomials as coefficients of a polynomial; this entry shows that the subalgebra those coefficients generate equals the one generated by the power sums of the roots — the full symmetric subalgebra in characteristic 0.
